title: publish-release.sh reads REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS and PROPAGATION_CUSHION_SECONDS into $(( )) unvalidated, the mechanism LCLI-626 fixed in readme-readback.sh
description: Found by the LCLI-626 delta reviewer (2026-09-28): the same mechanism in a second host. scripts/publish-release.sh sets REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS="${REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS:-1800}" and uses it in deadline=$(( started + REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS )) inside wait_for_all_visible, under set -uo pipefail (no -e) and macOS /bin/bash 3.2. PROPAGATION_CUSHION_SECONDS is read the same way and is unexamined. The reviewer's isolated 3-line probe under /bin/bash 3.2 showed 30m giving "value too great for base" with execution continuing to the next line. NOT measured on the real script: its behaviour on a malformed value (a wrong wait, an early exit, or a silent skip of the visibility gate) is unknown, and measuring it is the first step. LCLI-626 fixed readme-readback.sh by refusing any value outside ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,8})$ before anything is read, with a fixed verdict line and the value shown only printf %q escaped; promote-latest.mjs exports that grammar as REGISTRY_WINDOW.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The real script's behaviour on a malformed REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS and PROPAGATION_CUSHION_SECONDS is measured under /bin/bash 3.2 and recorded here before any fix
publish-release.sh refuses a malformed value of either variable before any registry read or publish, with a non-zero exit; a test drives it under /bin/bash 3.2 and asserts nothing was published
The accepted grammar matches readme-readback.sh and promote-latest.mjs REGISTRY_WINDOW (one grammar, pinned by a test)
bun test, bun run lint:shell and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the scripts change
